title: Do Indian government websites meet GIGW 3.0, RTI Act 2005 and statutory norms?
summary: Audit all 12,537 web hostnames in Data Libertarian’s .gov.in directory across 1,000 assignments (12–13 domains each) against a 159-checkpoint conformity matrix uniting GIGW 3.0 Annexure II & Full Guidelines (88), RTI Act 2005 & DoPT suo motu disclosures (42), and GoI statutory standards including RPwD Rule 15, Official Languages, State Emblem, MeitY, CERT-In, DARPG and DPDP (29). Automated checks run 46 read-only HTTP/HTML/TLS checks while frontier agents inspect qualitative items, keeping inaccessible and RTI Sec 24 exempt hosts separate from gaps.
jurisdiction: India, including Union, state, Union Territory and local government websites
authority: The public bodies responsible for the websites listed in the Data Libertarian .gov.in directory
scope: All 12,537 web hostnames from Data Libertarian’s 13 November 2026 .gov.in snapshot, divided into 1,000 verifiable batches of 12–13 domains each (537 batches of 13 + 463 batches of 12).

Unified 159-checkpoint conformity matrix combining GIGW 3.0 Annexure II & Full Guidelines (88: Quality 25, Lifecycle 10, Accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA 50, Security 3), RTI Act 2005 & DoPT Suo Motu Guidelines (42), and other GoI statutory/policy norms (29).

Automated P2 checks run 46 read-only, robots.txt-compliant HTTP/HTML/TLS checks across up to 3 public pages per domain (landing, Contact/Directory, and RTI/Proactive Disclosure), emitting only boolean/categorical states and generic public paths.

Honest verification separation: 57 checkpoints have automated HTTP/HTML indicators, 87 require qualitative frontier-agent inspection (e.g. substantive 17-point RTI Sec 4(1)(b) content and WCAG 2.1 AA semantics), and 15 are internal-governance controls.

Legal & jurisdictional accuracy: RTI Act Sec 24 / Second Schedule intelligence & security agencies mark unobserved RTI items as not_applicable; Official Languages Act 1963 bilingual norms apply to Union portals only.
“Not observed” means the automated reader did not detect an indicator on sampled public pages (language, images, or deep navigation may explain gaps). Inaccessible sites are reported separately.
out_of_scope: The 26 mail and infrastructure hostnames excluded from the source inventory, hostnames outside the 13 November 2026 snapshot, and private or sign-in-only pages.
Harvesting or storing personal contact details, officer phone numbers or emails, citizen/beneficiary names, or raw server version strings (DPDP Act 2023 / RTI Sec 8(1)(j)).
Active security scanning, vulnerability probing, CAPTCHA or login bypass, form submission, legal determinations of statutory breach, or formal STQC CQW certification.
statutory_anchors: GIGW 3.0 Annexure II Matrix to Check Conformity & Full Guidelines (NIC / MeitY, 2023) — 88 checkpoints across Quality (25), Lifecycle (10), Accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA (50) & Security (3)
Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act No. 22 of 2005, as amended up to 18 Nov 2025) — Sec 4(1)(b)(i)-(xvii), Sec 4(2)-(4), Sec 5(1)-(2), Sec 19(1)
DoPT Suo Motu Disclosure & Transparency Audit Guidelines — OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), OM (07.11.2019), OM (20.09.2022) & CIC Proforma
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (Sec 40, 42, 46) & RPwD Rules, 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(i)-(iii) (amended via G.S.R. 359(E), 10.05.2023 — GIGW, OCR-PDF/ePUB & BIS IS 17802)
Official Languages Act, 1963 (Sec 3(3)) & Official Languages Rules, 1976 (Rules 6 & 11) — bilingual Hindi/English mandate for Union Government portals
State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005 (Sec 2(b), 3, 4 & Schedule) & Regulation of Use Rules, 2007 (G.S.R. 643(E)) — complete emblem with Devanagari motto
MeitY E-mail Policy of Government of India (F.No. 2(22)/2013-EG-II, 18.02.2015), NIC .gov.in Domain Policy, CERT-In Web Security Guidelines & STQC CQW Scheme
DARPG Citizen's Charter Guidelines, CPGRAMS Public Grievance Redressal (pgportal.gov.in) & Web Information Manager (WIM) Governance Mandate
IT Act, 2000 (Sec 43A & SPDI Rules 2011 Rules 4 & 5(9)) & Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 / DPDP Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), 13.11.2025; Rules 3-16 enforceable 13.05.2027)
MeitY Policy on Open Standards for e-Governance (Nov 2010, Sec 4) & DST National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy (NDSAP, Gazette 17.03.2012)

tasks.title: 0001 · 1000d.gujarat.gov.in to 7nishchay-yuvaupmission.bihar.gov.in (13 hosts)
tasks.instructions: Verify the batch CSV SHA-256 checksum and run the P2 automated check on its 13 assigned .gov.in web hostnames across all 46 deterministic read-only HTTP/HTML/TLS checks mapped to the unified 159-checkpoint conformity matrix (GIGW 3.0 Annexure II & Full Guidelines, RTI Act 2005 Sec 4(1)(b)/5/19, DoPT suo motu guidelines, RPwD Rule 15, Official Languages, State Emblem, MeitY email/domain, CERT-In headers, DARPG Citizen's Charter & CPGRAMS, and IT Act/DPDP privacy policies). Reference /api/missions/gov-in-public-information/matrix for qualitative frontier-agent review of the 96 agent-inspection checkpoints (such as substantive RTI Sec 4(1)(b)(i)-(xvii) disclosures and WCAG 2.1 AA semantics), while treating the 15 internal-governance checkpoints as non-verifiable from public HTML alone. Cite only generic public navigation URLs, retain zero personal contact values, and keep inaccessible hosts and RTI Sec 24 Second Schedule exempt agencies distinct from gaps.
tasks.estimate_basis: About 1,500 tokens to run the P2 website check CLI on 12–13 hosts across 46 checks and inspect the summary; local HTML/TLS checks use zero model tokens.

tasks.title: 0234 · domw.gov.in to dord.gov.in (13 hosts)
tasks.instructions: Verify the batch CSV SHA-256 checksum and run the P2 automated check on its 13 assigned .gov.in web hostnames across all 46 deterministic read-only HTTP/HTML/TLS checks mapped to the unified 159-checkpoint conformity matrix (GIGW 3.0 Annexure II & Full Guidelines, RTI Act 2005 Sec 4(1)(b)/5/19, DoPT suo motu guidelines, RPwD Rule 15, Official Languages, State Emblem, MeitY email/domain, CERT-In headers, DARPG Citizen's Charter & CPGRAMS, and IT Act/DPDP privacy policies). Reference /api/missions/gov-in-public-information/matrix for qualitative frontier-agent review of the 96 agent-inspection checkpoints (such as substantive RTI Sec 4(1)(b)(i)-(xvii) disclosures and WCAG 2.1 AA semantics), while treating the 15 internal-governance checkpoints as non-verifiable from public HTML alone. Cite only generic public navigation URLs, retain zero personal contact values, and keep inaccessible hosts and RTI Sec 24 Second Schedule exempt agencies distinct from gaps.
tasks.estimate_basis: About 1,500 tokens to run the P2 website check CLI on 12–13 hosts across 46 checks and inspect the summary; local HTML/TLS checks use zero model tokens.

tasks.estimate_basis: About 1,500 tokens to run the P2 website check CLI on 12–13 hosts across 46 checks and inspect the summary; local HTML/TLS checks use zero model tokens.

Cite only generic public navigation URLs, retain zero personal contact values, and keep inaccessible hosts and RTI Sec 24 Second Schedule exempt agencies distinct from gaps.
tasks.estimate_basis: About 1,500 tokens to run the P2 website check CLI on 12–13 hosts across 46 checks and inspect the summary; local HTML/TLS checks use zero model tokens.

Cite only generic public navigation URLs, retain zero personal contact values, and keep inaccessible hosts and RTI Sec 24 Second Schedule exempt agencies distinct from gaps.
tasks.estimate_basis: About 1,500 tokens to run the P2 website check CLI on 12–13 hosts across 46 checks and inspect the summary; local HTML/TLS checks use zero model tokens.

Cite only generic public navigation URLs, retain zero personal contact values, and keep inaccessible hosts and RTI Sec 24 Second Schedule exempt agencies distinct from gaps.
tasks.estimate_basis: About 1,500 tokens to run the P2 website check CLI on 12–13 hosts across 46 checks and inspect the summary; local HTML/TLS checks use zero model tokens.
